title: Book Two · Chapter 148: The Soup and the List
story:
The holiday begins with a hot week. Ronan writes a daily reading plan with six neat lines. He shows it to Mum before breakfast.

She reads the first line, then the last.

“When do you eat?”

“Between these.”

“When do you see your friends?”

“I can fit that in.”

“Where?”

He points to an empty edge.

Mum gives the plan back. “You need time for meals and friends too.”

Ronan feels annoyed. He takes the plan to the step and looks at it again.

Leo arrives late in the morning. His family has another trip to the other town soon. He can stay for lunch today if Mum agrees.

Mum agrees. She asks the boys to wash vegetables while she starts soup.

Ronan puts the plan on a dry shelf. Leo sees it.

“Six lines?”

“Only six.”

“Six very long lines.”

They wash the greens. One leaf sticks to Leo's wrist. He holds it up.

“Does this count as lunch?”

“Only if you eat your wrist.”

Leo makes a face and drops the leaf into the bowl.

Ronan turns the greens in the water. A little sand lies at the bottom of the bowl.

“Done,” Leo says.

Mum looks in.

“Once more, please.”

Leo lifts the greens while Ronan changes the water. This time they put the bowl between them so neither has to reach across the other.

Ronan looks toward his plan on the shelf. The second line is waiting. He can see the neat words from here.

“Do you need that?” Leo asks.

“Not in the soup.”

Leo laughs. He puts the last clean leaves beside the pot. Ronan dries the wet part of the table, and Mum moves the hot pot into its place.

The three bowls do not fit around it at first. Ronan puts his own bowl at the end. Leo takes the chair beside him.

Now Ronan can see the whole table. He cannot see the six lines on the shelf, and he leaves them there.

At lunch, they talk about the trip. Leo will visit the school on a normal school day before it closes for its holiday. His parents have arranged the visit.

“Will you come back before our next term?” Ronan asks.

“Yes. I am starting next term here.”

Ronan feels better. Leo will still be at their school next term.

“But later?” he asks.

“Still not sure.”

Mum passes the soup. “One answer at a time.”

After lunch, the boys read a short funny page together. Then they go to the square with Dad for half an hour. Ronan does not finish the second line of his plan until evening.

He expects to feel far behind. Instead he remembers Leo's leaf wrist and a good catch near the wall.

At the table he takes out a clean page. He copies two short reading times. He leaves room for home jobs, friends, and free afternoons. He does not fill every space.

Dad looks over his shoulder.

“Where is the soup?”

“In the middle.”

“A good place.”

Mum checks the page and gives it back. “You can change it when life changes.”

Ronan puts the old six-line plan beneath his notebook. It is not a promise to anybody else. The new plan looks less impressive. But he has time for a story, a game, and lunch now.

Before bed, he reads one whole story for pleasure. He does not write its words in a list. He tells Mum the funny part, and she laughs before he reaches the end.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

daily＝每天的；arrange＝安排；impressive＝让人印象深的；pleasure＝乐趣。

## 理解问题

1. 六行计划忽略了哪些生活内容？
2. Leo对下一学期给出了什么确定信息？

## 读句子

**Mum / passes / the soup.** Mum／把汤／递过去。
